Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

- Key constraints: single-tenant VPC, TLS termination at customer edge, integration with your KMS for keys.
- Engineering ask: you said your infra team will validate network topology and share a sample request/seq-length distribution by EOD Thursday.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: latency targets and next steps

Alex / Marissa —

Following up with the numbers from our internal perf run that aligns with Acme Bump's profile. High-level:

- Test config: 4x A100s (dedicated), batch sizes tuned to hit 10k qps aggregate, typical prompt length 120 tokens (avg), generation 512 tokens.
- Observed: p50 = 48ms, p95 = 132ms, p99 = 210ms for 512-token generation under steady 10k qps when using continuous batching and KV cache warm.
- Throughput: sustained ~10.8k tokens/sec per GPU (aggregate depends on shard config); see attached throughput table for per-GPU breakdown.
- Notes: quantized_v2 model variant shows ~1.6x improvement in throughput with ~1-2% degradation in exact-match for some narrow tasks; happy to run a quick eval if you care about task-level quality trade-offs.

Attachments: redwood_latency_report_acme_100k_tokens.pdf (summary, charts), redwood_throughput_table_acme.csv (per-GPU breakdown)

Quoted below is Marissa's recap for context:
